title: Spectral Dragon Photography Studio
description: An antique camera sits on a pedestal in a dark studio, aimed at a dragon that shimmers with a custom chromatic dispersion shader. The user adjusts shader parameters through interactive controls—manipulating refraction index, dispersion strength, fresnel power, chromatic aberration offset, and glow intensity—then triggers the antique camera to 'capture' the dragon, freezing the current shader state into a polaroid-style snapshot that slides out from the camera with a film-grain post-processing effect.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a Spectral Dragon Photography Studio. Load DragonDispersion.glb and AntiqueCamera.glb using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Place the AntiqueCamera model on the left side of the scene on a small pedestal, angled toward the center. Place the Dragon model in the center, slightly elevated and slowly rotating on a turntable. Use a dark studio environment with three colored SpotLights (warm key, cool fill, rim light) to create dramatic lighting. Write a custom ShaderMaterial applied to the dragon mesh that simulates chromatic dispersion. The vertex shader should pass world-space normals and view direction to the fragment shader. The fragment shader must implement: (1) a refraction effect using a uniform refractionIndex (range 1.0-2.5, default 1.33), (2) chromatic aberration splitting RGB channels by a uniform dispersionStrength (range 0.0-0.15, default 0.05), (3) a Fresnel rim glow controlled by uniform fresnelPower (range 0.5-5.0, default 2.0), (4) a chromatic offset uniform chromaticShift (range 0.0-0.1, default 0.02) that shifts the RGB sample directions apart, and (5) a glow intensity uniform glowIntensity (range 0.0-3.0, default 1.0) that multiplies the Fresnel rim color. Use an environment map or a simple cubemap for refraction sampling. Create an HTML/CSS overlay panel with five labeled sliders for these uniforms, each showing its current numeric value. Add a 'Capture Photo' button. When clicked, animate the antique camera with a subtle shake using GSAP or manual tweening, play a shutter-click sound effect via AudioContext, then render the current scene to an offscreen RenderTarget, apply a film-grain post-processing pass using EffectComposer and a custom ShaderPass, and display the result as a polaroid-style thumbnail that slides in from the camera's position to the bottom-right corner of the screen. Validate that each slider updates its corresponding uniform in real time and that the capture button only works after at least three sliders have been changed from their defaults. Use OrbitControls locked to a 45-degree vertical arc. The scene background should be a dark gradient.
